tasks.short: Prepare and issue invoices, credit documents and shipping labels from approved transaction records.

steps.what: Gather order, delivery, customer and price records from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Check billing data for missing references, duplicate charges and inconsistent quantities in the {ERP}.
Generate the invoice and verify totals, tax treatment and payment terms in the {ERP}.
Prepare a credit document against the original invoice in the {ERP}.
Approve or reject the credit reason and amount in the {ERP}.
Post validated invoices and approved credits in the {ERP}.
Create shipping labels from the dispatch record in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Send posted billing documents through {EMAIL} and retain delivery evidence.

tasks.design: Configure the {ERP} to validate billing data, generate documents, post eligible transactions and issue them through approved channels. A deterministic integration supplies delivery records from the {OPS_SYSTEM}; credit decisions and failed checks enter a focused approval queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fragmented order and delivery records, inconsistent reference data and undocumented credit permissions prevent reliable straight-through processing.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document templates and posting controls cover most arithmetic. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building missing mappings and validation rules.
tasks.still_hard: Tax exceptions, disputed delivery evidence, incomplete addresses and commercial credit decisions still need accountable owners.
tasks.human_edge: Understand why a charge or credit is justified when transaction records conflict with the commercial agreement.

ambition.what: Pre-dispatch billing readiness checks for the dispatch team

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving billing exceptions before dispatch. They gain authority to clear documented data defects within agreed limits; credit approval remains with the finance manager.

reach.task: Reconcile invoice postings to revenue and tax accounts.
reach.learn: Posting logic, tax codes, reconciliation evidence and period cutoffs.

evidence.claim: Invoice arithmetic, templates, posting rules and dispatch labels are established deterministic software capabilities.
The proposed outgoing billing workflow and its time savings are estimates, not documented outcomes from the digest.

assumptions: This baseline represents a mid-size European company using an {ERP} and an {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Shares describe pooled effort across invoices, credits and labels; these are conditional branches, not steps every case follows.
Routine invoice posting and delivery can use pre-authorised rules; credits require a separate decision.
Build ranges cover one entity and a limited document set, using supported interfaces.
GDPR applies to customer data. Assess EU AI Act obligations if model features are later added; national rules determine consultation requirements.
Consent and access time includes a consultation assessment and any required employee consultation; elapsed waiting may exceed working-day estimates.
unknowns: Available interfaces, licences and existing automatic billing features.
Actual document mix, volumes, exception rates and time shares.
Applicable tax jurisdictions and structured invoice requirements.
Credit limits, approval roles and permissions for automatic issue.
Whether employee consultation is required for the proposed changes.
research_questions: Which requirements for invoice format, retention and delivery apply in the target jurisdictions?
Can native configuration cover the validation and document lifecycle before custom code is needed?
new_work: Resolve failed validations and delivery failures.
Maintain document templates, tax mappings and credit approval limits.
Monitor duplicate prevention, posting reconciliation and interface failures.

tasks.short: Answer and route calls, arrange appointments, and order routine office supplies.

steps.what: Answer calls through {TELEPHONY}, provide basic information and transfer specialist questions.
Collect appointment purpose, participants and timing constraints through {EMAIL}.
Find an acceptable slot and send the invitation through {CALENDAR}.
Select supplies from the approved catalogue and create a requisition in {PROCUREMENT}.
Approve the requisition against budget and purchasing policy in {PROCUREMENT}.
Issue the approved purchase order through {PROCUREMENT}.

tasks.design: Configure structured appointment requests in {WORKFLOW}, availability rules in {CALENDAR}, and catalogue requisitions and approval routing in {PROCUREMENT}. Keep live calls with the clerk, supported by a maintained directory in {DOCS}, and issue purchase orders only after the recorded purchase decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Small administrative requests arrive through different channels, and scheduling or purchasing rules often live in people's heads.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, calendar settings and purchasing workflows handle much of the work. Faster configuration and integration make small administrative improvements easier to justify.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent interruptions, unavailable participants, unusual equipment and ambiguous calls require contextual decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise urgency, reassure callers and negotiate competing demands on people's time.

ambition.what: Self-service appointment requests for external service partners

tasks.altitude: The clerk handles fewer scheduling exchanges and repeated purchase entries. They can resolve standard scheduling conflicts within agreed priorities; spending authority does not change.

reach.task: Check purchase order references when invoices arrive.
reach.learn: Cost centres, purchase approval limits and receipt evidence.

evidence.claim: Forms, availability rules, catalogue requisitions and approval routing can be configured without autonomous agents.
The digest reports a vendor case moving purchasing approvals out of an executive's inbox; it does not establish savings for this whole task.

assumptions: Calls, appointments and purchasing are independent branches; shares represent their pooled effort.
The baseline company already uses {CALENDAR} and catalogue purchasing in {PROCUREMENT}.
Appointment intake can become structured; unusual requests remain with the clerk.
No call recording or worker scoring is introduced.
GDPR applies to participant and caller data. National rules determine any employee consultation; EU AI Act obligations must be assessed if AI features are added.
Build ranges assume existing licences and include access review, consultation assessment and any required employee consultation.
unknowns: Actual call, scheduling and purchasing volumes.
Calendar visibility and external booking restrictions.
Catalogue coverage, budget checks and approval limits.
Available configuration features and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which administrative requests can use existing forms and catalogues without custom integration?
Which scheduling exceptions need personal negotiation?
new_work: Maintain contact directories, booking rules and approved catalogue entries.
Handle incomplete requests and scheduling exceptions.
Monitor duplicate orders and failed invitations.

tasks.short: Contact customers to clarify account details, explain balances and record agreed follow-up.

steps.what: Review account balances, invoices and earlier contacts in the {ERP} and {CRM}.
Call the customer and verify identity and authority before discussing account information.
Clarify missing details, explain account entries and agree next actions with the customer.
Record the conversation outcome and assigned follow-up in the {CRM}.

loop.input: Clerk-written conversation notes and permitted follow-up categories.
loop.output: A proposed account note, action owner and due date.
loop.check: Require source text for each commitment; validate identifiers and dates; the clerk approves the record.
loop.stop: One extraction and one schema repair maximum; missing commitments or failed checks return to manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes vary; fixed fields alone do not reliably capture the agreed action.

steps.what: Send a written account explanation or information request through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A read-only integration combines the {ERP} ledger and {CRM} history into a source-linked account brief. A bounded extraction loop prepares notes from the clerk's written summary, while configured templates prepare follow-up through {EMAIL}; the clerk approves saved notes and outgoing messages.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ledger details and contact history sit apart, and staff repeatedly rewrite conversation outcomes.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic joins can assemble account facts, while a small model loop can turn variable notes into proposed fields with explicit review.
tasks.still_hard: Identity verification, disputed facts, customer frustration and unauthorised commercial commitments remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Find the real reason for confusion and reach a workable next action without promising an unsupported adjustment.

ambition.what: Proactive first-invoice explanation calls for new customers

tasks.altitude: The clerk enters conversations with a complete account brief and spends less time recording them. They can prioritise clarification calls and close routine information gaps; settlement and credit authority do not change.

reach.task: Prepare disputed overdue accounts for collection follow-up.
reach.learn: Dispute ownership, payment-plan boundaries and escalation criteria.

evidence.claim: Onguard CreditManager supports configured reminder and call-campaign workflows, supporting routine follow-up rather than autonomous customer conversations.
Combining account records and extracting proposed actions from clerk-written notes is technically feasible; the proposed savings remain estimates.

assumptions: The baseline is a clerk-led telephone conversation with written follow-up; local channel mixes vary.
The {ERP} and {CRM} share a reliable customer identifier.
The model receives clerk-written notes, not recorded calls, and cannot change balances or promise concessions.
Routine account contact is distinct from creditworthiness assessment; adding that purpose requires a separate EU AI Act assessment.
GDPR requires appropriate access, processing arrangements and retention. National rules determine consultation requirements.
Build ranges include access review, consultation assessment and any required employee consultation; lengthy procurement is excluded.
unknowns: Actual contact channels, conversation lengths and dispute rates.
Permitted model processing environment and retention settings.
Who may correct customer master data or agree account adjustments.
Employee consultation requirements and approved response templates.
research_questions: What verification procedure is appropriate for each contact channel and disclosure type?
Can structured note templates provide sufficient benefit before introducing extraction?
new_work: Review extracted commitments, owners and dates.
Maintain response templates and follow-up categories.
Resolve unmatched customer records and stale account data.
Sample note accuracy and investigate unsupported extracted statements.

tasks.short: Review operating costs and revenue to prepare rate recommendations for approval.

steps.what: Export operating costs, revenue and service volumes from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Reconcile periods, service categories and allocation inputs in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Calculate unit costs, margins and rate scenarios in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Interpret rate scenarios and document a recommendation in {DOCS}.
Review commercial effects and approve proposed rates with the finance manager.
Enter approved rates and effective dates in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations load reconciled costs, revenue and service volumes into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with configured scenarios displayed in {BI}. The clerk investigates exceptions and recommends changes; a recorded approval in {WORKFLOW} controls effective-dated rate updates in the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent service definitions, manual allocations and spreadsheet reconciliation make frequent analysis expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled data pipelines and configured calculations already handle the numerical work. AI-assisted coding can shorten the work of implementing mappings and reconciliation checks.
tasks.still_hard: Cost allocation, demand response, contract restrictions and pricing objectives require judgement; more frequent calculations do not resolve them.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a temporary cost spike from a structural pricing problem and explain the commercial tradeoff.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time investigating margin changes and testing assumptions. They gain discretion to select scenarios and escalate services for review; the finance manager retains rate approval.

reach.task: Test how service volumes and cost assumptions affect the operating forecast.
reach.learn: Fixed and variable costs, allocation drivers, sensitivity analysis and forecast reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Unit-cost calculations, scenario tables, scheduled refreshes and effective-dated rates can use deterministic technology.
The digest provides no documented case for this rate-setting workflow; implementation effort and time reductions are estimates.

assumptions: The clerk prepares analysis and recommendations; the finance manager approves rates.
Daily work mainly refreshes or reviews analysis; rate changes occur on an approved schedule.
Shares average preparation, review and publication across the rate-review cycle.
Existing {BI} calculations can express the agreed allocation and scenario rules without a model.
Build ranges cover one service hierarchy and agreed allocation rules.
GDPR applies where records contain personal data. No worker scoring or individual creditworthiness assessment is proposed; reassess EU AI Act obligations if scope changes.
Consent and access time includes consultation assessment and any required consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Whether this clerk recommends rates or has delegated rate-setting authority.
Allocation quality, service definitions and available volume records.
Contractual, regulatory and customer-notification restrictions on rate changes.
Existing {BI} capabilities, refresh requirements and approval mechanisms.
Access restrictions and applicable employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which allocation methods best represent the services being priced?
Which rate changes require contract review or customer notice before their effective date?
new_work: Maintain service mappings, allocation drivers and scenario assumptions.
Investigate reconciliation failures and unusual margins.
Check effective dates and prevent overlapping rate versions.
Compare approved scenarios with later realised costs and revenue.

role.altitude: The billing clerk moves from gathering records and entering documents toward resolving billing defects, clarifying customer accounts and investigating margins. They gain bounded authority over data corrections, exception priorities and scenario preparation; credit concessions, spending and rate approval remain with designated managers.
reach: Accountant: reconcile billing outputs to ledger and tax accounts.
Bill and account collector: prepare disputed accounts with clear evidence and ownership.
Budget analyst: investigate service margins and test forecast assumptions.
skills_to_grow: Billing controls, tax codes and reconciliation
Reviewing extracted notes and maintaining workflow rules
role.ambitious_version: Run a billing readiness and margin review service that catches missing evidence before dispatch, helps new customers understand their first invoice, and brings service-level pricing exceptions to the finance manager each week.
